A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MimicMotion and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. All pages were inspected, including v2's Appendices A-D; v1 ends with references and has no appendices. Renumbered and reformatted material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original TikTok benchmark results, qualitative component ablations and a 36-participant preference study.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds quantitative component ablations, additional comparison metrics and cartoon/animal generation examples.

M1.justification: The written output-assembly rule changes: v1's Listing 1 retains the complete first segment and skips the initial C frames of subsequent segments, whereas v2's Algorithm 1 returns each segment's first N-C frames. This is a limited revision to the specified procedure; an implementation change is not established. The backbone, confidence guidance and hand-loss mechanism remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds evaluation on four cartoon and four animal dancing videos, extending coverage beyond human subjects to different visual styles and body proportions. The human training collection and TikTok evaluation remain unchanged. This substantially broadens demonstrated domain coverage, although the added evidence is qualitative.

E2.justification: v2 adds MagicAnimate, printed as 'MagicAnymate' and identified by the Xu et al. reference, to Table 1's quantitative TikTok comparison. MagicPose, Moore and MuseV remain. The qualitative comparisons and preference chart retain their original comparator membership.

E3.justification: v2 adds SSIM and PSNR alongside FID-VID/FVD and introduces four quantitative component configurations in Table 2. The TikTok 335-340 split, central cropping, training budget and user-study size remain consistent. Newly stated clip lengths, noise parameters and display randomization document settings rather than establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: v1 supports its three components with qualitative ablations. v2 retains those examples and adds Table 2, measuring configurations that progressively enable fusion, confidence guidance and hand enhancement across four metrics. Appendix D also adds cross-domain transfer cases. These substantially strengthen component analysis and generalization evidence.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and the 36-participant, six-pairs-per-baseline user study are retained. Pose-confidence scores are method inputs, not experimental uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing FID-VID/FVD scores, including MimicMotion's 9.3/594, and user-preference percentages remain unchanged. v2 adds SSIM/PSNR results, including 0.795/20.1 for MimicMotion, the additional baseline's results, quantitative ablation outcomes and cartoon/animal outputs. Table 2 newly shows fusion alone improving FVD from 776 to 678 while slightly worsening the other metrics. These are additional findings, not performance gains over v1.

T1.justification: The diffusion preliminaries and denoising-loss mathematics are retained, with equations condensed or renumbered. No new theorem, proof or substantive theoretical derivation appears. Appendix A's noise-distribution formula documents a training setting.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: confidence-aware pose guidance, confidence-based hand enhancement and progressive latent fusion for long, temporally smooth videos. Condensed wording and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly attributes cross-domain generalization to a possible shared pose-feature subspace and limb-length mapping to reference characters. Section 4.3 adds interpretation of fusion's selective improvement in FVD despite other metrics not improving. The original explanations of pose robustness and hand enhancement remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds PoseNet's layerwise architecture, 576-by-1024 training resolution, 16-frame clips, noise-distribution parameters, 10:1 hand-loss weighting, six-frame overlap for the illustrated fusion comparison, and user-interface randomization details. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing retraining. Conversely, v1's explicit SVD 1.1 checkpoint designation, 40GB GPU specification and executable Merge listing are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including StableAnimator, ControlNeXt, DisPose, VividPose, DiT and noise-schedule research, plus sources supporting newly documented settings and metrics. DreamPose is removed. The central positioning relative to SVD, MultiDiffusion and Lumiere remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and numerous paragraphs across the introduction, preliminaries, architecture description and experiments are substantially condensed or rewritten. v2 adds organized Appendices A-D and an Impact Statement, and changes citation style. This is extensive editorial restructuring despite retention of the main scientific narrative.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference main text, with widespread resizing and relocation of figures. v1's confidence/occlusion illustration is removed; retained ablation figures are renumbered. Table 1 gains a comparator and metric columns, while Tables 2-3 and Figures 10-12 add ablations, architecture details, the study interface and cross-domain examples.

improvement.justification: v1 relies on selected visual examples for component ablations and describes PoseNet only broadly. v2's quantitative controls in Table 2 and detailed training/architecture specifications in Appendices A-B substantially improve the central contributions' evidential support and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the loss of some checkpoint and merge details. Cross-domain evidence remains qualitative, and statistical uncertainty reporting remains absent.
